\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرعت} (sor'at)}{سرعت (sor'at)}]{\fa{سرعت} (sor'at) — speed}

\label{lesson:FA-C424-sorat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to run out, then the Persian for a car wash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرعت}}
\textbf{\fa{سرعت}} (\emph{sor'at}) — \textquotedblleft{}speed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سرعت} \fa{این} \fa{قطار} \fa{خیلی} \fa{زیاد} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sor'at-e in qatâr kheyli ziyâd ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This train's speed is very high.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâ sor'at} — quickly, at speed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sor'at} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{surʿa} 'speed, haste' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sor'at}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sor'at}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sor'at}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to run out, then the Persian for a car wash, then say \emph{sor'at} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفتن} (sor'at gereftan)}{سرعت گرفتن (sor'at gereftan)}]{\fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفتن} (sor'at gereftan) — to speed up, to gather speed}

\label{lesson:FA-C424-sorat-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a car wash, then the Persian for speed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{sor'at gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to speed up, to gather speed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{شهر} \fa{اتوبوس} \fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az shahr otobus sor'at gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the town the bus sped up.
\end{quote}

\emph{sor'at} + \emph{gereftan} (to take). Present stem \emph{gir-}: \emph{sor'at migirad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sor'at gereftan} is built from \emph{sor'at} 'speed', borrowed from Arabic \emph{surʿa} (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take', which is usually traced to Old Persian \emph{grab-} 'to seize'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sor'at gereftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sor'at gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sor'at gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a car wash, then the Persian for speed, then say \emph{sor'at gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سرعت} \fa{گرفتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To speed up, to gather speed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سبقت} \fa{گرفتن} (sebqat gereftan)}{سبقت گرفتن (sebqat gereftan)}]{\fa{سبقت} \fa{گرفتن} (sebqat gereftan) — to overtake (US: to pass)}

\label{lesson:FA-C424-sebqat-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for speed, then the Persian for to speed up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سبقت} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{سبقت} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{sebqat gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to overtake (US: to pass)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{پیچ} \fa{هیچ} \fa{وقت} \fa{از} \fa{اتوبوسها} \fa{سبقت} \fa{نمیگیرم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar pich hich vaqt az otobus-hâ sebqat nemigiram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I never overtake buses on a bend.
\end{quote}

\emph{sebqat} 'going ahead' + \emph{gereftan}; the one overtaken takes \emph{az}: \emph{az u sebqat gereft}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sebqat gereftan} is built from \emph{sebqat} 'getting ahead', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{sabq} 'going ahead, a race', and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take'. EtymDB lists \emph{sebqat} without a source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sebqat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sebqat gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sebqat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for speed, then the Persian for to speed up, then say \emph{sebqat gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سبقت} \fa{گرفتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To overtake (US: to pass)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کنار} \fa{زدن} (kenâr zadan)}{کنار زدن (kenâr zadan)}]{\fa{کنار} \fa{زدن} (kenâr zadan) — to pull over (to the side of the road)}

\label{lesson:FA-C424-kenar-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to speed up, then the Persian for to overtake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کنار} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{کنار} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{kenâr zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to pull over (to the side of the road)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{راننده} \fa{کنار} \fa{زد} \fa{و} \fa{ما} \fa{پیاده} \fa{شدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rânande kenâr zad va mâ piyâde shodim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver pulled over and we got out.
\end{quote}

\emph{kenâr} (side, edge) + \emph{zadan}. \emph{Kenâr zadan} can also mean to push something aside.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kenâr zadan} is built from native \emph{kenâr} 'side, edge', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{kanārag}, and the native verb \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kenâr zadan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to speed up, then the Persian for to overtake, then say \emph{kenâr zadan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ایمنی} (imeni)}{ایمنی (imeni)}]{\fa{ایمنی} (imeni) — safety}

\label{lesson:FA-C424-imeni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to overtake, then the Persian for to pull over.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ایمنی}}
\textbf{\fa{ایمنی}} (\emph{imeni}) — \textquotedblleft{}safety\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کمربند} \fa{برای} \fa{ایمنی} \fa{مسافران} \fa{مهم} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kamarband barâ-ye imeni-ye mosâferân mohem ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The belt matters for the safety of the passengers.
\end{quote}

\emph{Kamarband-e imeni} — a seat belt. Built on \emph{imen} 'safe' + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{imeni} is built from \emph{imen} 'safe, secure' and the noun ending \emph{-i}. \emph{Imen} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{āmin} 'safe, secure'; EtymDB does not list \emph{imen} or \emph{imeni}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
